index_title: Fresh real frames, actual quotient-fibre avoidance and hereditary unary SAP
scope: Private B039: FIVE Foundations I results and THREE auxiliary equations, including the previously unexpanded homogeneous unary SAP criterion as a SELECTED extra result. Expand generic fresh-frame/orbit equivalence, simultaneous avoidance in ONE actual quotient fibre, the relative-kernel sufficient criterion and its exact converse. Import ONLY the abstract finite-action avoidance proof from B010, not its CCO/owner geometry. The AFF construction itself uses neither homogeneous/countable H nor real-base orbit infinitude; those premises enter only the acl/dcl/SAP conclusion. No CCO, original SAP, lattice geometry, HN/HKN theorem or new external provider input.
scope_explanation: statement and proof. Distinguish the actual subgroup G from full Aut(H), actual fibre image cardinalities from abstract subgroup indices, and a NAMED unary factor term from a mere set-theoretic factor. Conditional implication claims explicitly discharge their temporary orbit/SAP premises when assembled.

assumptions.name: Typed unary closure without nullary generators
assumptions.statement: H is a many-sorted structure with arbitrary relations; every named function is UNARY and TOTAL on its specified source sort. There are NO nullary generators. The closure of every finite set under well-sorted unary terms is finite (for the fibre lemma finite singleton closures suffice). Include the identity term on every sort; closures are sets of actual vertices, and the empty closure is empty.

assumptions.name: Actual automorphism subgroup
assumptions.statement: G is an actual subgroup of Aut(H), preserving all named sorts, relations and unary functions. Every named unary term is G-equivariant. G need not equal the full automorphism group, be closed, countable or faithful.

assumptions.name: Invariant generating union of real sorts
assumptions.statement: For the generic frame equivalence, R is a G-invariant union of named real sorts and every vertex of H is a unary term value of some point of R. Every finite A therefore has a FINITE real generating cover. No transitivity or homogeneity is assumed in this branch.

assumptions.name: Generic SAME-G real-base orbit condition
assumptions.statement: For every finite D subset R and every u outside cl(D), the ACTUAL orbit G_D.u is infinite. This is the standing premise for fresh frames => closed-base orbit infinitude; the reverse direction needs only its stated closed-base orbit premise and does NOT use A04.

assumptions.name: Independent homogeneous unary age setting
assumptions.statement: For the unary SAP criterion H is COUNTABLE and HOMOGENEOUS for finite induced unary-CLOSED substructures. Age(H) is the isomorphism-closed class of all such finite substructures. No finite-language, oligomorphic, CCO, original SAP or real-sort generation assumption is needed by this criterion. Algebraicity means finite full-Aut stabiliser orbits, and definability means singleton such orbits.

assumptions.name: One ACTUAL named quotient of a transitive real sort
assumptions.statement: G is transitive on named real sort M. p_J:M->Q is a NAMED surjective equivariant unary projection with actual kernel equivalence J STRICTLY ABOVE Id_M. For each actual well-sorted unary term tau:M->H_s, K_tau is its actual kernel. The relative index [J:J meet K_tau] means the number of K_tau-classes meeting one J-class, equivalently |tau(p_J^-1(b))|; transitivity makes it independent of b. It is NOT a formal subgroup index or a division of cardinalities.

assumptions.name: Literal named factorisation for FORCED terms
assumptions.statement: For EVERY actual real-source unary term tau with J<=K_tau, there exists an ACTUAL NAMED well-sorted unary term sigma:Q->H_s such that tau=sigma composed p_J on ALL M. A set map constant on fibres, even a definable one, does not replace this term premise.

assumptions.name: Infinite relative index for UNFORCED terms
assumptions.statement: For EVERY actual real-source unary term tau with J not<=K_tau, the actual fibre image cardinality [J:J meet K_tau] is infinite. The identity term is included, has kernel Id_M and is unforced because J>Id_M. No finite-only experiment establishes this hypothesis.

assumptions.name: Retained homogeneous finite-language theorem scope
assumptions.statement: For the FINAL theorem/corollary scope retain countable homogeneous oligomorphic H in a FINITE named language, with A01 total typed unary functions, no nullary generators and finite unary closures. This supplies the homogeneous criterion A05, but is NOT an active premise of the narrower AFF construction C28-C33.

assumptions.name: Main theorem FULL-Aut real-base orbit condition
assumptions.statement: For every finite original real D and every vertex u of H (real or nonreal) outside cl(D), Aut(H/D).u is infinite. This is about FULL Aut(H), not necessarily the smaller transitive subgroup G. It is used after AFF to conclude acl=dcl=cl and hereditary SAP, not to construct the fresh frame itself.

assumptions.name: Finite original real-sort family and actual named representations
assumptions.statement: G<=Aut(H) is transitive on each of FINITELY MANY named original real sorts M_a. Every NONREAL hidden vertex b has a representation b=p_J(x) for a NAMED surjective equivariant actual quotient p_J:M_a->Q_(a,J), J>Id_a. For the sufficient criterion apply A06-A08 to every such projection and actual term. Real vertices need no nonidentity quotient representation. This supplies real generation and the FINITE real-sort family; no homogeneity, countability, oligomorphy, CCO or SAP is assumed here.

imports.name: Abstract simultaneous finite-action avoidance
imports.statement: For ANY group action, finite moving set S with every orbit infinite, and finite forbidden Z, there is ONE g sending ALL S outside Z. Reuse ONLY the elementary coset-cover proof; empty S/Z and nonfaithful actions are allowed. No topology, CCO, real closure, owner geometry or EPPA premise is imported.
imports.provider_support_usage: C01 proves the abstract virtual-containment preorder and C02 proves the finite coset-cover lemma; they are strict proved ancestors of C03, which converts forbidden action incidences into transporter cosets and yields simultaneous avoidance. Extract their abstract group/action hypotheses only, never CCO/owner branches.

definitions.name: Actual unary closure
definitions.statement: cl(T) is all well-sorted named unary term values of points of T, INCLUDING identity terms. With no nullary generators cl(empty)=empty; arbitrary finite unions of closed sets are closed.

definitions.name: Pointwise stabilisers and closure equivariance
definitions.statement: G_T fixes EVERY point of T; Aut(H/T) uses the full automorphism group. Unary term equivariance gives g cl(T)=cl(gT) and equality of stabilisers for T and cl(T).

definitions.name: Orbit-theoretic acl and dcl
definitions.statement: acl_G(T) consists of vertices with finite G_T-orbit, and dcl_G(T) those with singleton orbit. Unsubscripted acl_H/dcl_H use FULL Aut(H). The packages do not switch subgroup orbits to full-Aut orbits silently.

definitions.name: Fresh real frame separation
definitions.statement: For every finite induced unary-closed A subset B there exists finite D subset R with A subset cl(D) and cl(D) intersect B=A. D may include real A points; no functorial or canonical frame is required.

definitions.name: Closed-base orbit infinitude
definitions.statement: For every finite unary-closed A and every u outside A, G_A.u is infinite. This condition itself is the conditional antecedent in the reverse frame implication; no SAP of a subgroup action is presumed.

definitions.name: Hereditary unary-closed age and strong amalgams
definitions.statement: Objects are ALL finite induced unary-closed substructures, including those not generated by real points. SAP asks for induced embeddings of any closed span with factor images intersecting exactly in the base. Arbitrary cross relations are those induced from a host; no FREE-amalgamation conclusion is asserted.

definitions.name: Actual term kernel and quotient fibre
definitions.statement: K_tau={(x,y):tau(x)=tau(y)}; J=ker(p_J). For b in Q let F_b={x:p_J(x)=b}. These are actual G-invariant equivalences and an actual nonempty fibre.

definitions.name: Relative fibre index
definitions.statement: [J:J meet K_tau]=|tau(F_b)|, equivalently the number of (J meet K_tau)-classes in a J-class. Uniformity follows from actual transitive G. No commutation/exact lattice or formal numerical quotient is used.

definitions.name: Typed term functions and evaluation at one real point
definitions.statement: Consider distinct actual functions tau:M->H_s induced by all named well-sorted terms, retaining output sorts. In a many-sorted disjoint carrier equality of their value at x0 forces same output sort; transitivity/equivariance determine their entire function.

definitions.name: Forced and unforced terms
definitions.statement: A term is FORCED when J<=K_tau and UNFORCED otherwise. A07 supplies a named factor sigma and forced value sigma(b) in cl({b}); A08 supplies infinite G_b-orbits of unforced values.

definitions.name: Finite sequential representative request
definitions.statement: For a finite list of represented quotient vertices, choose real representatives one at a time; the next finite forbidden set may contain an extra finite hidden set, previous representatives and their previous unforced term values. Forced coincidences are retained rather than forbidden.

definitions.name: Relative-kernel condition RK
definitions.statement: Over EVERY named actual quotient and EVERY actual real-source term, require named factorisation in the forced case and infinite actual fibre index in the unforced case, together with full-Aut real acl=cl. This is a precise signature-dependent condition, not quantification over all conceivable equivariant maps.

claims.name: Unary closures are singleton unions, including the empty case
claims.statement: cl(T)=union_(t in T) cl({t}); every term follows one generator and identity includes it. No constant term contributes at empty T. Thus finite unions of closed sets are closed, and finite singleton closures imply finite closures of finite sets. Arbitrary relations do not change closure.

claims.name: Automorphisms commute with closure and stabilisers coincide
claims.statement: For every g in G, g tau(t)=tau(gt), so g cl(T)=cl(gT). Every g fixing T fixes all term values, and T subset cl(T); hence G_T=G_cl(T). The same argument holds for FULL Aut(H).

claims.name: Term closure is pointwise definable before any orbit hypothesis
claims.statement: Every unary term value over T is fixed by its full-Aut stabiliser, giving cl(T) subset dcl_H(T) subset acl_H(T). The analogous inclusions hold for any subgroup G. No homogeneity, real generators or orbit infinitude is needed.

claims.name: Fresh frame separation implies closed-base infinite orbits
claims.statement: CONDITIONAL on fresh frames D04, fix finite closed A and u outside A. B=cl(A union {u}) is finite closed. Choose D with cl(D) intersect B=A. Thus u outside cl(D), A subset cl(D), and A04 gives infinite G_D.u. Since G_D<=G_A by term-fixing, G_A.u is infinite. This implication uses SAME-G A04 and real generation scope, no SAP/homogeneity.

claims.name: Closed-base infinite orbits imply fresh frames by one common move
claims.statement: CONDITIONAL on D05, choose finite real D0 generating a cover of finite closed A by A03. S=cl(D0) minus A is finite; every G_A orbit of S is infinite. Apply I01 once to S and Z=B minus A, giving g in G_A with gS disjoint Z. Put D=gD0 subset R. Closure equivariance and g fixing A give A subset cl(D) and cl(D) intersect B=A. This direction does NOT need A04.

claims.name: Generic fresh-frame equivalence and all finite hidden bases
claims.statement: Under A01-A04, C04/C05 prove the stated equivalence. WHEN EITHER equivalent condition holds, for arbitrary finite T subset H, C02 identifies G_T with G_cl(T). Every closure point is fixed; every point outside has infinite orbit by the closed-base condition. Hence acl_G(T)=dcl_G(T)=cl(T), with no homogeneity/SAP needed.

claims.name: Full-Aut SAP does not imply an arbitrary subgroup orbit condition
claims.statement: SAP of Age(H) refers to full-Aut stabilisers through the separate homogeneous criterion. A proper subgroup may have finite off-closure orbits even in an infinite pure set with SAP (take the trivial subgroup). It fails A04, so does not refute C06; it guards against dropping that actual subgroup premise.

claims.name: The age and induced union use unary closed substructures
claims.statement: In the A05 setting, an induced substructure on a unary-closed subset of a finite age object is again in the age. A finite union of two actual closed sets in H is closed by C01; higher-arity relations may cross factors and are inherited from H without affecting closure. This is hereditary closed age, not only real-generated objects or a free relational union.

claims.name: Conditional SAP builds arbitrarily many disjoint off-base copies
claims.statement: IF Age(H) has SAP, fix finite closed A and u outside A; B=cl(A union {u}) is finite closed. Repeatedly strongly amalgamate n B-copies over ONE common A. Strongness makes their u-images pairwise distinct; the finite host may have extra vertices. Embed that age host into H and use homogeneity to align the embedded A pointwise with literal old A.

claims.name: Homogeneity puts each copied point in the actual base orbit
claims.statement: After C09 alignment, each B-copy is induced-isomorphic to the literal old B over A, so homogeneity extends it to a FULL automorphism fixing A and sending u to its distinct copy. Thus for every n the actual Aut(H/A).u orbit has at least n points.

claims.name: SAP implies infinite closed-base orbits
claims.statement: The C09/C10 construction for every finite closed A and off-base u proves that conditional SAP implies infinite full-Aut closed-base orbits. The proof needs age embeddability and homogeneity; it does not assume finite language, oligomorphy or any real-base property.

claims.name: Put an arbitrary closed span inside H over its exact common base
claims.statement: For any finite closed span A->B1,B2, embed both age objects in H. The two induced copies of A are isomorphic; homogeneity aligns their bases via one automorphism. Relabel them as actual B1,B2 inside H with the same literal A. No assumption yet requires disjoint off-base parts.

claims.name: Infinite closed-base orbits separate the two whole factors
claims.statement: IF every off-closed-base full-Aut orbit is infinite, act with Aut(H/A) on S=B2 minus A and forbidden Z=B1. I01 supplies ONE g moving all S outside B1 while fixing A. Consequently B1 intersect gB2=A. Empty S or A are permitted; no element-by-element choice replaces the common automorphism.

claims.name: Their induced unary-closed union is a strong age amalgam
claims.statement: The finite induced host on B1 union gB2 is unary-closed by C08/C01 and belongs to Age(H). Its inclusions are induced embeddings, with intersection A by C13. This proves SAP; cross relations may be present, so it is not a free amalgam assertion.

claims.name: Infinite closed-base orbits imply hereditary SAP
claims.statement: C12-C14 work for EVERY finite induced unary-closed span, hence the conditional closed-base orbit criterion implies SAP of the entire hereditary unary-closed age. No prior original real SAP is supplied.

claims.name: Homogeneous unary SAP criterion with acl and dcl
claims.statement: C11/C15 give SAP iff infinite off-closure orbits over finite closed bases. C02 identifies full-Aut stabilisers of T and cl(T), and C03 fixes all closure values; therefore this is equivalent to acl_H(T)=cl(T) for EVERY finite hidden T. In that case dcl_H(T)=cl(T) too. This expands the selected upstream lemma and equation UA internally.

claims.name: Fresh-frame remark follows for the FULL automorphism group
claims.statement: In the A01/A03/A05 setting with full-Aut real acl=cl, C06 applied to full Aut(H) and C16 identify fresh frames, acl=cl on EVERY finite hidden base, and SAP of the WHOLE hereditary closed age. The named real sorts are full-Aut invariant. This expands the explanatory remark without counting it as a numbered result.

claims.name: Only finitely many distinct real-source term functions
claims.statement: Fix x0 in transitive M. All term values tau(x0) lie in finite cl({x0}). If two typed term functions agree at x0, choose g with gx0=y for arbitrary y; equivariance gives agreement at y. Thus evaluation at x0 INJECTS distinct actual term functions into cl({x0}), although syntactically there may be infinitely many terms.

claims.name: The quotient-point stabiliser is transitive on its actual fibre
claims.statement: For x,y in F_b, transitivity of G on M gives g with gx=y. Named projection equivariance gives gb=g p_J(x)=p_J(y)=b, hence g belongs to G_b. Conversely a G_b move of x stays in F_b. No surjectivity onto the full automorphism group is used.

claims.name: Term-value orbit equals its actual fibre image
claims.statement: For x0 in F_b, G_b.tau(x0)=tau(F_b) by C19 and term equivariance. Distinct values correspond exactly to K_tau-classes inside F_b, giving actual relative cardinality D08. G-transitivity also transports this cardinality between fibres. No commuting lattice or subgroup-index theorem enters.

claims.name: Finitely many unforced values each have infinite stabiliser orbit
claims.statement: Take the finite SET S of all unforced term values tau(x0), finite by C18. A08 and C20 give infinite G_b-orbit for each value. Coincident values or repeated syntax require no extra representative; the moving set need not be a union of orbits.

claims.name: One fibre-stabilising automorphism avoids every unforced value
claims.statement: Apply I01 to G_b acting on H, moving S of C21 and arbitrary finite Z. Obtain ONE g fixing b and sending every S outside Z. Put x=gx0. Then p_J(x)=b and EVERY unforced tau satisfies tau(x)=g tau(x0) outside Z. Independent choices for different terms would not suffice.

claims.name: Forced term values are literally named closure values of b
claims.statement: For a forced tau, A07 gives tau=sigma p_J on ALL M, so for EVERY x in F_b its value is sigma(b) in cl({b}). These prescribed values may lie in Z and must be retained; they are not avoidance requests. This uses actual named factorisation, not just constancy on the fibre.

claims.name: Exact closure intersection equality, not only containment
claims.statement: Every point of cl({x}) is a real-source term value. If in Z, C22 forces that term to be forced, so C23 puts it in cl({b}). Conversely b=p_J(x), a named term value, gives cl({b}) subset cl({x}) by term composition. Therefore cl({x}) intersect Z=cl({b}) intersect Z.

claims.name: The identity term guarantees the representative itself avoids Z
claims.statement: The identity term on M has actual kernel Id_M. As J>Id_M, it is unforced and included in C22, so x is outside Z. Without strict nonidentity J this conclusion would fail for a forbidden singleton fibre; no separate infinite-fibre premise is silently added.

claims.name: Successive choices keep requests finite and allow forced coincidences
claims.statement: For finitely many quotient vertices, possibly different transitive real sorts, repeat C22-C25 with forbidden sets enlarged by any finite hidden set, all earlier real representatives and all their unforced term values. Finite singleton closures C01 keep every next request finite. Representatives become pairwise distinct; forced values may coincide and are retained. No simultaneous disjointness of all closures is claimed.

claims.name: Actual quotient-fibre avoidance source export
claims.statement: C22-C26 give one common representative for ALL actual term functions, the exact closure intersection and finite sequential choices. This branch needs only unary singleton finiteness, actual transitive G quotient, named forced factors and infinite unforced fibre indices. No homogeneity/countability/real-base orbit/SAP premise is used.

claims.name: Start the main fresh frame with the actual real points of A
claims.statement: For finite closed A subset B, D0 is the finite set of ORIGINAL REAL vertices in A. Because A is unary-closed, cl(D0) subset A. No assertion says A must already be real-generated internally; its nonreal points may need representatives outside A.

claims.name: Choose actual named quotient representations for every nonreal A point
claims.statement: Enumerate all nonreal b_i in A and use A11 to choose b_i=p_(J_i)(x_i^0). Their full singleton closures are contained in A by its closedness. Real generation of H follows by representing every nonreal vertex and using identities on reals; no canonical representative choice is needed.

claims.name: Choose each representative fresh relative to B and all prior requests
claims.statement: Apply C27 in each prescribed quotient fibre, with Z containing all B, earlier representatives and optionally their earlier unforced values. The new x_i is outside B and all prior representatives. Every term value in B is forced, and belongs to cl({b_i}) subset A by C23/C24. Forced values in A remain permitted.

claims.name: The real union generates every point of A
claims.statement: Let D=D0 union {x_i}. Each real A point lies in D0 and each nonreal b_i is the named projection of its chosen x_i. Hence A subset cl(D), with D finite and original real. This is real generation by a fresh cover, not A being generated by its own real points.

claims.name: Singleton union proves AFF with exact empty-base behaviour
claims.statement: By C01, cl(D) is the union of the generator singleton closures. D0 closures are contained in A; every x_i closure meets B only in A by C30. Along with C31, cl(D) intersect B=A. If A is empty there are no generators and cl(empty)=empty; if A has only real points use D=A. This proves equation AFF.

claims.name: AFF construction is independent of homogeneous orbit assumptions
claims.statement: The proof C28-C32 uses actual quotient representations, transitive G, finite unary singleton closures, A07/A08 and I01 only. It does NOT use A10, homogeneity, countability, finite language or oligomorphy. Retain those extra structural premises for the source theorem export but do not import its final SAP conclusion into this construction.

claims.name: AFF transfers FULL-Aut real-base infinitude to arbitrary closed bases
claims.statement: Fix finite closed A and u outside A and set B=cl(A union {u}). C32 provides finite original real D with A subset cl(D), u outside cl(D). A10 gives infinite Aut(H/D).u; this stabiliser fixes A by term-fixing, so Aut(H/A).u is infinite. This is the C04 mechanism instantiated with FULL Aut, requiring no infinite orbit under the smaller G.

claims.name: Relative-kernel sufficient criterion gives hidden acl=dcl=cl and SAP
claims.statement: For arbitrary finite hidden T use C02 and C34: closure points are fixed and off-closure points have infinite FULL-Aut stabiliser orbit. Thus acl_H(T)=dcl_H(T)=cl(T). A09 supplies the homogeneous setting of C16, which gives SAP of the entire hereditary closed age. Combine with C32 AFF for the complete theorem export.

claims.name: Uniform singleton bound is derived without an arbitrary-base bound
claims.statement: On each transitive real sort M_a, automorphisms carry singleton closures bijectively by C02, so their finite sizes are constant. There are finitely many original real sorts, hence their maximum is finite (empty list is vacuous). C01 gives at most this bound times the number of real generators, not a bound independent of |D|. Oligomorphy/finite language are retained source scope, not needed for this elementary fact.

claims.name: For the converse assume SAP, not the kernel dichotomy
claims.statement: CONDITIONAL on SAP in the structural A09 setting, C16 gives acl_H(T)=dcl_H(T)=cl(T) for EVERY finite hidden T. In particular full-Aut real-base equality holds. Neither A07/A08 nor A10 nor the sufficient AFF construction is assumed in this direction.

claims.name: A forced fibre value is fixed by FULL Aut over its quotient point
claims.statement: Fix actual p_J,tau with J<=K_tau, choose x in M_a, b=p_J(x),v=tau(x). For EVERY h in Aut(H/b), named p_J gives hx in the SAME ACTUAL fibre, so tau(hx)=tau(x) and hv=v. This uses fibre constancy, not a named factor premise; no full-Aut transitivity or equality G=Aut(H) is assumed.

claims.name: SAP forces a named unary term realising that fixed value
claims.statement: Under conditional SAP, C38 puts v in dcl_H({b}) subset acl_H({b})=cl({b}) by C37. With no constants, singleton closure is EXACTLY named unary term values, so some actual well-sorted sigma satisfies v=sigma(b). The term identity is allowed if the output sort is Q.

claims.name: One equality extends to the global literal factor by transitive G
claims.statement: CONDITIONAL on an actual named sigma satisfying tau(x)=sigma(p_J(x)) at ONE x, transitivity/equivariance give the global factor. For arbitrary y choose g in G with gx=y, so tau(y)=g tau(x)=g sigma(p_J(x))=sigma(p_J(y)). Applying this general fact to C39 yields the forced clause under SAP. The local-to-global implication itself assumes no SAP or A07.

claims.name: A nonforced actual kernel has at least two values on every fibre
claims.statement: If J not<=K_tau, some J-fibre contains two points with different tau values. Actual G-transitivity transports that fibre to any chosen b, so the common relative cardinal r=|tau(F_b)| is at least two. In a hypothetical finite-index case r is a positive finite integer >=2.

claims.name: Finite fibre image is full-Aut invariant and hence algebraic over b
claims.statement: In the hypothetical r<infinity case, V_b=tau(F_b) has exactly r elements. Every h in Aut(H/b) preserves named p_J and tau, hence permutes V_b, even when h is outside G. Therefore v=tau(x) has finite FULL-Aut orbit over b, putting it in acl_H({b}).

claims.name: G_b transitivity shows that value lies outside named closure
claims.statement: C19/C20 make G_b transitive on V_b. As r>=2, some g in G_b moves v. Every named unary term value of b is fixed by G_b, so v is outside cl({b}). This uses actual G action only to witness nonfixing, not to identify its finite orbits with full-Aut orbits.

claims.name: SAP rules out every finite proper relative index
claims.statement: C42 gives v in acl_H({b}), while C43 puts v outside cl({b}), contradicting C37. Thus every unforced term has INFINITE actual relative fibre index. Along with C40, this proves both kernel clauses without assuming either one.

claims.name: The reverse condition instantiates the sufficient theorem exactly
claims.statement: CONDITIONAL on RK D12 including real acl=cl, closure term-fixing C03 shows the real-base orbit condition A10. The named forced and infinite unforced clauses instantiate A07/A08. The structural assumptions are unchanged, so C35 gives SAP. This is a conditional use of the already expanded sufficient theorem, not an extra external provider.

claims.name: Exact relative-kernel characterisation source export
claims.statement: C37/C40/C44 prove SAP=>real acl=cl plus BOTH RK clauses for EVERY existing named quotient and actual real-source term. C45 proves the converse. No separate original CCO, SAP, distributive/exact lattice, kernel commutation or real-base orbit input is required by the FORWARD implication. Quantifying over actual named terms is essential.

claims.name: Missing named forced factor gives a definable off-closure value
claims.statement: Without assuming SAP, let tau be constant on fibres but have NO named sigma factor. A11 transitivity implies tau(x) cannot equal ANY sigma(b), for such equality would globalise as in C40. Thus v is outside cl({b}), while C38 fixes it under full Aut(H/b). This is a local definable-off-closure witness, not an appeal to a nonexistent factor term.

claims.name: Finite proper relative index gives an algebraic off-closure value
claims.statement: Without assuming SAP, any actual unforced finite index 2<=r<infinity yields C42 finite full-Aut orbit and C43 moving G_b witness, hence v in acl_H({b}) minus cl({b}). It is a local obstruction over ONE quotient vertex and does not require building a global bad span first.

claims.name: Set-theoretic factorisation alone is insufficient and finite controls cannot prove infinity
claims.statement: For countably infinite Q and M=Q times an infinite pure fibre, a separate copy S of Q, named p:M->Q and tau:M->S with a named relation matching Q to S but no unary Q->S map, tau is constant on p-fibres. Its set/definable factor exists, yet cl({q}) misses the matched s. In a 2-cover V->Q with named swap, and infinite M->V fibres, p:M->Q,tau:M->V give actual relative index TWO; over real bases all off-closure orbits can still be infinite. These are two distinct local failures. Finite growing models diagnose their closure/action mechanism only, never certify A08 or unbounded infinitude.

claims.name: Unary and no-nullary restrictions protect the exact construction
claims.statement: A named constant adds a closure point even at empty base, changing C01/C32 bookkeeping. A binary function can take one argument from each factor, making an induced union nonclosed and generating mixed values in cl(D); the C14/C32 proof is unary-specific. These delimit the proof mechanism, not a claim that no other theorem can handle broader signatures.

frame_contracts.SAP_criterion: C08-C16: full Aut, whole hereditary closed age
frame_contracts.term_finiteness: C18: actual functions, not syntactic terms
frame_contracts.simultaneous_choice: C22: ONE g for ALL unforced terms
frame_contracts.named_forced_terms: C23; a set-theoretic factor is insufficient
frame_contracts.AFF: C28-C33: no A10 or orbit/SAP conclusion
frame_contracts.forced_converse: C38-C40: full-Aut fixing, then transitive G globalisation
frame_contracts.finite_index_converse: C41-C44: full-Aut invariant finite set plus moving G_b
frame_contracts.all_external_bindings: Existing THREE HN and TWO HKN bindings unchanged; no new external theorem

Finite controls are diagnostics and cannot establish infinity. No CCO or external HN/HKN premise may enter.
